description.narrative: CREA, is an international feminist women´s human rights organisation based in New Delhi. CREA builds feministic leadership and movements, works for women´s human rights and to expand sexual and reproductive freedom.

Creating Resources for Empowerment and Action Inc, CREA är en internationell feministisk kvinnorättsorganisation baserad i New Delhi, Indien. CREA har inkommit med en förfrågan om stöd på 20 miljoner kronor för en period på fyra år (2016-2019). Detta för att stödja deras Strategiska plan 2015-2020. Ett kärnstöd till CREAs aktiviteter möjliggör för organisationen att uppnå dess strategiska prioriteter och mål.
CREAs strategi syftar till att bygga feministiskt ledarskap och rörelser, arbeta för kvinnors mänskliga rättigheter och för att expandera sexuell och reproduktiv frihet. CREAs arbete följer i huvudsak tre strategier: 1) bygga ledarskapskapacitet, kunskap och färdigheter för i huvudsak aktivister från små, rättighetsbaserade organisationer i syd genom att tillhandahålla kapacitetsbyggande kurser, studieresor och utbytesprogram. 2) Stärka feministiskt ledarskap och rörelser genom att bygga kapacitet för kvinnor att ställa upp i val, att utöva sin rösträtt och engageras sig i beslutsprocesser samt stärka deras ledarskap och möjlighet att mobilisera samhället runt frågor som påverkar kvinnor och flickor. 3) Utöka kunskap och skapa en resursbas från ett sydperspektiv, och utöva påverkan för förändring av lagar, policyer genom nätverkande och samarbete med andra.
I relation till den globala/tematiska resultatstrategin bedömer Sida att relevansen i att stödja CREA är tydlig. Enheten INTEM/DEMO har identifierat behovet av att öka stöd till jämställdhet och till sydbaserade organisationer som når gräsrotsnivån. CREAs mervärde ligger i det faktum att organisationen är sydbaserad och arbetar utifrån ett sydperspektiv med nära koppling till gräsrotsnivån. Detta mervärde blir särskilt tydligt när det gäller frågor som är politiskt och kulturellt känsliga som jämställdhet, sexuella rättigheter inklusive HBTI personers rättigheter då dessa ibland uppfattas som introducerade och ålagda utifrån västerländska värderingar. CREA har ett tydligt fattigdomsperspektiv och rättighetsperspektivet genomsyrar deras arbete.
CREAs totala budget för strategiperioden 2015-2020 är ca 229,190,000 SEK. För närvarande har CREA ca 108,617,000 SEK i säkrade medel med Sidas stöd inräknat.

Strategic Objectives
Strategic Objective 1: Feminist leadership and movements are strong, intersectional, inclusive, and amplify the voices of structurally excluded people.
Strategic Objective 2: Sexual and reproductive health and rights are advanced so that all people exercise bodily autonomy, consent and control over their choices and decisions.
Strategic Objective 3: Responses to gender-based violence expand and promote well-being, security and rights.
Strategic Objective 4: Feminist, human rights and allied movements defend and expand civic space and foster collective resilience.
Strategic Objective 5: CREA manifests its values to be an intersectional, inclusive, accessible, diverse, innovative, collaborative and multigenerational feminist organisation that strives to operate at high levels of excellence, effectiveness and accountability.

sector.narrative: Women’s rights organisations and movements, and government institutions

description.narrative:
Summary of results 20162021 based on CREA's final report
Strategic Initiative 1: Feminist leadership and movements are strong, intersectional, inclusive, and amplify the voices of structurally excluded people.
In the reporting period, CREA hosted 13 Feminist Leadership, Movement Building and Rights Institutes (FLMBaRI), one of CREAs pivotal programmes in South Asia and the MENA region. The Institute brings together women leaders and activists to strengthen feminist leadership and collective power for social transformation. CREA reports that FLMBaRIs have facilitated progressive shifts in the knowledge and analysis of feminist leaders and activists on a range of key issues such as GBV, rights of persons with disabilities, LBT persons and persons in prostitution, womens leadership, among others. CREA also reports that the FLMBaRI participants and faculty members continue to network with and learn from each other. This has granted relevance to the work and learning of participants far beyond the duration of the actual Institute.
CREA launched the South Asia Young Womens Leadership and Mentorship (SAYWLM) initiative in 2017, in partnership with the Global Fund for Women. SAYWLM is a unique model of structured mentoring of a new generation of feminist leaders. The programme mentors 30 Young Women Leaders (YWLs) from 30 womens rights organisations in India, Bangladesh, and Nepal. Once trained, these 30 women then build the capacity of 300 Community Young Women Leaders (CYWLs). SAYWLMs cohort of mentors also help YWLs sustain south-south feminist collaboration. CREA reports that two predominant levels of impact as been observed movement building and enhanced leadership capacities of YWLs. An endline survey conducted by CREA (2020) found that all YWLs self-identified as leaders and attributed this to SAYWLM. 44% of YWLs marked a considerable increase in their assertion of rights in family spaces, while all of them improved their capacities in community mobilisation.
CREA initiated the New Voices/New Leaders programme in 2013 to provide an opportunity for mutual learning and exchanges between womens organisations from Burma/Myanmar and Nepal. CREA reports that several organisations from Myanmar have integrated concepts (such as power, feminism and feminist leadership) in their trainings, while drawing upon the resource material offered by CREA's trainings. For close to two decades, CREA has worked with a network of 32 community based, grassroots organisations. CREA reports that the network has succeeded in enhancing the perspective and skill building of local activists on gender, sexuality, GBV, and sexual and SRHR in India. Over the last two years, Ibtida has focused on capacity and feminist leadership building of Elected Women Representative in India. CREA reports that between 20162021, over 100 grassroots organisations and Ibtida members attended CREAs capacity building trainings. Between 20162021, Ibtida members collaborated with CREA to engage with over 5,000 EWRs to strengthen their advocacy skills for support of women and girls in their communities. CREA reports that many girls have started to stall their early marriages to complete their education while some others tried to know their sexual identities by connecting with organisations working on sexuality.
In 2015, CREA began the SELF Academy in rural India as a 10day Residential programme for young girls. The objective was to build their skills, confidence, and self-reliance, especially with matters related to their bodies, health, and career, via life affirming and genderbending sports. A majority of these girls belong to the most structurally excluded communities. By 2019, CREA expanded the SELF programme to East Africa. CREA reports that 21 girls and young women graduated from the SELF Academy in Machakos, Kenya in 2019, and 154 girls and young women graduated from the SELF Academy in India from 2016 to 2020. CREA reports that the SELF academy has enabled girls to access public spaces like never before. A large number of them now teach football to other girls in the village, while some work as football coaches. The DSROI is a six week long, online Institute that CREA started in 2010. The motive was to share a right based, conceptual understanding of disability and sexuality, and their interlinkages with feminism, public health, violence from a global South perspective. Between 2016 and 2021, 145 people attended 3 DSROI Institutes. CREA reports that participants of the Institute have reported gaining and/or building an intersectional perspective on gender, race, class, sexuality and disability, within the context of human rights policies and laws for persons with disabilities. It also built bridges between different People with Disability and Disabled Persons Organisation across countries and fostered networks for collective advocacy.
Strategic Initiative 2: Advanced sexual and reproductive health and rights
CREAs Sexuality, Gender, and Rights Institutes (SGRIs) employ creative teaching and learning methodologies to push the analytical bar on issues of and around sexuality and gender, and enable participants to apply their newfound understanding in their respective work areas. CREA reports that most participants report the SGRI to be a progressive awakening to a compendium of issues such as sex workers rights, disability and sexuality. After over a decade of SGRIs, in 2016 CREA strengthened connections between 20 SGRI alumnae from its global community by forming the SGRI Alumni Forum. This facilitated cross learning, collective strategizing for advocacy of sexual rights, and promotion of crossmovement knowledge building. Since 2005, CREA has actively engaged with CSW, CEDAW, CRPD, COSP and Generation Equality Forum as well as co-leading Action Coalition 6. CREA's work with the United Nations Human Rights Council (UNHRC) in Geneva is operational on multiple levels. CREA reports that during the 33rd session of the UNHRC, CREA submitted a report for Indias UPR to advocate for sexual and reproductive health and rights of women with disabilities and the uncoupling of sex work and trafficking. Both these were recorded in the compilation of UN information. At the 37th session, CREA made statements after the Special Rapporteur on Disabilities presented her report on legal capacity and the High Commissioner on Human Rights presented his report on access to justice for people with disabilities. Moreover, CREA reports that its side events at different UN platforms and gatherings ensured cross movement and cross regional representation, and safe access and participation for structurally excluded women. Despite attempts by many member States to dilute the language in the resolutions on SRHR the SRICREA partnership helped in the inclusion of strong language. For example, during the 40th session in 2019, CREA offered inputs on language for/around hyperandrogenism and sex verification in sports (in the resolution on elimination of discrimination against women and girls in sport). CREAs It's My Body (IMB) programme works with adolescent girls and young women who belong to structurally excluded communities such as Scheduled Tribes, Scheduled Castes, other excluded classes, and minorities in India. The mission of the programme is to affirm and promote their rights via training on SRHR, gender, sexuality, and bodily autonomy through sports. Between 2016 and 2021, over 7584 girls (aged 1216 years) participated in the IMB. CREA reports that In 2019, CREA increased the duration of the programme from 10 months to 18 months to intensify the strengthening of the collectives of girls and women. This led to a deeper interface between young girls and EWRs, and finally to girls greater understanding and articulation about their rights at meetings with health service providers, community leaders, and school teachers. IMB alumnae are able to break their conditioning of silence, challenge discriminatory norms of gender and sexuality, and motivate other girls to play and learn with them.
Strategic Initiative 3: Responses to gender-based violence expand and promote well-being, security and rights.
CREA is part of the CMI! Consortium, made up of five feminist organisations and womens funds working globally on issues of gender based violence, economic justice and sustainable resourcing. Its objective is to address stark gender inequalities and violence against women that persists in South Asia and East Africa. In 2019, as part of CMI, CREA helped build capacities of feminist activists and organisations for direct lobbying and advocacy in national and global policy spaces on GBV against structurally excluded groups. Through different CMI initiatives, over 14000 persons in prostitution led or participated in initiatives on awareness raising, mutual skill building, information and experience sharing, and mobilisation.
The All Women Count! (AWC) consortium is an alliance of four human rights organisations that are globally networked with diverse human rights movements and have deep programmatic experience in the global South. It aims to strengthen the ability of global South based human rights organisations to respond to GBV by changing harmful social norms and building the capacity of women and girls (including trans people, women with disabilities and persons in prostituion) to combat violence. CREA reports that during 2016- 2020, as part of AWC, CREA built the capacity of 127 girls and young women through SELF Academies in India and attended to 489974 calls on online infoline calls.
Moreover, over the past 5 years, 13 855 participants of AWC initiatives improved their capabilities in campaigning, public education and awareness raising on GBV and implementing GBV programmes.
Strategic Initiative 4: Increase voice and visibility of marginalised people
CREA reports that SRHR of women with disabilities is a marginal issue not just in the agenda of disability rights organisations, but also among women´s rights and feminist organisations and movements. CREA has taken some pioneering steps towards developing the discourse around this intersectional practice among its constituency of partners and donors during the agreement period. CREA reports that Between 2016 and 2021, CREA built the institutional capacity of DPOs and women's rights organisations to address sexuality and disability. CREA and one of its partners conducted two needs assessment exercises as well as several workshops with parents, activists, academics, students, and professionals. As a result, participants gained a comprehensive perspective on the interconnections of gender/sexuality and disability, including questions of law, social movements, accessibility, abortion, marriage, sexualities, the market and popular media. CREA reports that its big and growing global signature across continents and cultures implies crosscutting dialogue and connections. Over the years, this has led to both consolidation of its perspectives and as well as the expansion of vision. CREA states that as a result of CREAs active contribution to the collaborative drafting process of the Feminist Declaration in 2020 (on the occasion of the 25th anniversary of the Fourth World Conference on Women), the position and language of the Declaration is in favour of persons in prostitution groups and other partners. This led to an entire section in the final version of the Feminist Declaration being dedicated to the protection of the rights of sex workers. CREA also ensured attention to sexual and gender diversity across all sections of the Feminist Declaration, and to the threat of global anti gender and rightwing movements.
In 2019, CREAs second global conference "reconference" was a coming together of activists, artists and allies to deeply reflect upon injustice and change. Participants discussed subjects such as abortion rights, sports, consent, disabilities, environmental justice and technology. This feminist expo was at the intersection of academia, art, and activism. The reconference was attended by more than 700 participants from over 63 countries, representing 180 organisations, reflecting the significance of diversity and inclusiveness CREA highlights. CREA reports that the ability of reconference to intersect feminist scholarship with feminist activism proved to be a valuable learning for attendees. Participants from across the globe experienced it as a rich opportunity to strengthen alliances and network, especially through cross movement collaborations.
Finally, CREA reports that it has ensured that lesbian, trans and gender nonconforming/ nonbinary people are a part of, and leaders in, global Southled networks and capacity building initiatives for sexual and gender diversity. CREA has also integrated a broad understanding of sexual and gender diversity into all its Institutes, programming, and publications.
The information above is mainly based on reports including the final report for the years 2016- 2021. The programme was extended for one year and CREA was to submit one more annual report after the final report. Results from the final year are included below.
Reports 2022/2023 This reporting year´s results presented in numbers include: 8 CREA Institutes with 267 people attended these institutes, 105 training sessions/trainer of trainers with 1597 people attended trainings, 175 knowledge products generated of which 23 were produced in a language other than English, 135 Art music, sports and other inpersons events and 34,854 people attended these events, 29 Online events not including trainings or institutes with 570 people attended online events and 72 subgrants to organisations.
CREA reports on having delivered 8 training institutes with a total of 267 participants. The institutes held live includes Sexuality, Gender, and Rights Institute (SGRI) Global Feminist Leadership Movement Building and Rights Institute (FLMBaRI) South Asia FLMBaRI Hindi and SGRI Hindi. Online Institutes includes the Disability, Sexuality and Rights Online Institute (DSROI)in Hindi and adapted contexually for East Africa and Our Voices Our Futures (OVOF) Tech Deepdive, based on expanded digital accessibility practices. CREA included statements from participants in the report showing increased understanding and transformation in thinking.
CREA started its first Fellowship in 2022, CREAte a result of the goal of expanding the methods of generating, collectivizing, and sharing knowledge creatively with the intention of generating deeper understanding and connections between sexual and gender diversity, intersex rights, disability work and movements by supporting production and knowledge, art and storytelling. Six selected CREAte fellows facilitated learning sessions on disability justice and project implementation sessions and created diverse projects with a global south perspective. Examples of results include a booklet in English and Portuguese on the intersectionality between invisible disabilities and gender and sexual diversity which combines scholarship, storytelling and poetry and a campaign focusing on ableist GBV against queer women and trans and nonbinary persons with disabilities which will be a resource for other organisations working on similar issues. Another example is a collection of stories, in English and Tamil of living at the intersection of intersex rights, caste, gender and sexual diversity and disability (the first book in Tamil to explore intersectional issues in Tamil Nadu).
Within the area of movement building CREA reported on partnerships and contributing to building networks. Women Gaining Ground (WGG) a consortia that CREA leads and OVOF expanded work in their second year. As part of WGG CREA hosted the East Africa chapter of the SELF Academy together with Akii Dada and Femme Fort. The Count Me In! (CMI!) consortium continued and CREA supported multiple cross movement gatherings and highlighted results from that in the annual report. CREA joined a new consortium, Feminist Opportunities Now, with International Planned Parenthood FederationAfrica Region (IPPFAR) as the lead, to expand work in feminist movement building and fight gender based violence (GBV). Since 2018 CREA has been partnering with the Korean Institute for Gender Equality Promotion and Education a government affiliated organisation. This year CREA worked with CREA consultant to prepare six training modules for understanding disability and gender. CREA also led short sessions on disability and sexuality for donors, i.e for the staff of the American Jewish World Services and staff of the Malala Fund.
A new collaboration was started with the New York Times to develop a story on disability rights, sexuality and consent. Within media work CREA also produced audio/visual contend i.e. "think Feminist podcast ant the "Think CREA: Feminist Journeys" video talk series. The last two were a response to demand for Institute resources. The podcast had 1820 all time plays and 179 followers at the time of reporting. CREA was also in several engagements with the aim of bringing together the sexual and gender diversity movements, i.e. ILGA world conference and the Conference of State Parties to the UN Convention on Rights of Persons with Disabilities. As part of the global advocacy work CREA is supporting the development and implementation of the Feminist Accessibility Protocol a joint initiative with Women Enabled International and the Inclusive Generation Equality Collective ,the protocol is a step towards ensuring the participation of feminists with disabilities in international advocacy spaces.
